title: Illumination for computer generated pictures
method_summary: Phong compares shading rules and relates image quality to normals, hidden-surface removal and perception.
project_comparison: The project evaluates lighting per fragment. It uses the Blinn half-vector variant rather than copying Phong's original reflection-vector expression.

title: A Reflectance Model for Computer Graphics
method_summary: Cook and Torrance model reflection using surface microgeometry and material-dependent directional response.
project_comparison: This is the physical comparison for the vault's brass and painted metal. The implemented empirical Blinn-Phong shader is cheaper and easier to explain, but it does not reproduce a calibrated metal BRDF.

title: An Inexpensive BRDF Model for Physically‐based Rendering
method_summary: Schlick develops a compact reflectance model that balances physical constraints with practical cost.
project_comparison: Its efficiency goal supports keeping material controls understandable. The game does not implement the full Schlick BRDF or claim physically based rendering.

title: Geometric skinning with approximate dual quaternion blending
method_summary: Kavan and colleagues replace linear matrix blending with approximate dual-quaternion blending to reduce collapsing-joint artifacts.
project_comparison: The thief uses linear blend skinning because its weights and motions are simple. This paper identifies a concrete future improvement for shoulder and knee volume preservation.

title: Fast and Efficient Skinning of Animated Meshes
method_summary: Kavan, Sloan and O'Sullivan fit standard linear skinning to animated meshes with sparse weights and efficient optimization.
project_comparison: The runtime likewise benefits from sparse influences and a compact palette. Our weights are authored procedurally and normalized, not fitted with the paper's optimization.

title: Smooth skinning decomposition with rigid bones
method_summary: Le and Deng jointly recover rigid bone transforms and sparse convex skinning weights from example poses.
project_comparison: Their nonnegative, normalized weight constraints motivate explicit export validation. The project keeps an authored anatomical hierarchy instead of performing skinning decomposition.

title: Efficient collision detection using bounding volume hierarchies of k-DOPs
journal: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
method_summary: Klosowski and colleagues organize discrete-orientation bounding volumes into hierarchies for efficient collision queries in complex environments.
project_comparison: A hierarchy is unnecessary for six laser boxes and a small set of furniture colliders. Transforming body samples into each beam's local space keeps the project inexpensive and directly inspectable.

title: 3D collision detection: a survey
method_summary: Jimenez, Thomas and Torras classify continuous and sampled collision strategies and explain how temporal and spatial pruning control cost.
project_comparison: The game adopts repeated static local-box tests at 240 Hz, with a conservative body margin. This is bounded sampling, not an exact continuous-collision solver for arbitrary velocities.

title: A survey of visibility for walkthrough applications
journal: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
method_summary: Cohen-Or and colleagues survey visibility algorithms for interactive walkthroughs, including techniques that avoid drawing hidden geometry.
project_comparison: The compact single room uses depth testing, back-face culling and static instancing. More complex occlusion systems would add overhead without a demonstrated benefit at this scene size.

title: Photographic tone reproduction for digital images
method_summary: Reinhard and colleagues adapt photographic tone reproduction to map high-dynamic-range images to a display.
project_comparison: The project also renders into a floating-point target before display conversion. Its implemented global fitted curve is credited separately and is not Reinhard's photographic operator.

title: A visibility matching tone reproduction operator for high dynamic range scenes
journal: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
method_summary: Larson, Rushmeier and Piatko preserve visibility through tone reproduction informed by luminance adaptation and human vision.
project_comparison: This provides a criterion for tuning the night scene: the safe and hazards must remain readable. The game uses artistic tuning rather than the paper's histogram and visual-adaptation model.

title: A Survey of Real‐time Soft Shadows Algorithms
method_summary: Hasenfratz and colleagues compare real-time shadow methods by geometry, lighting conditions, image quality and cost.
project_comparison: The vault uses one directional depth map with a small PCF kernel. The spotlights illuminate surfaces but do not each render a separate shadow map; their dust cones are an inexpensive visual approximation.

title: Collision Detection for Deformable Objects
method_summary: Teschner and colleagues survey deformable collision using hierarchies, distance fields, spatial partitioning, image-space and stochastic methods.
project_comparison: The animated thief is represented by a sampled upright body for gameplay. This avoids deforming triangle-level collision, while pose-bound checks keep the crouched mesh compatible with the chosen clearance.

title: Texture and reflection in computer generated images
method_summary: Blinn and Newell use surface parameterization to map patterns and filter their contributions over a pixel footprint.
project_comparison: The project's UV coordinates and mipmaps address the same sampling problem. Its mesh rasterizer does not reproduce the original patch renderer or environment-reflection system.

title: Parallel controllable texture synthesis
method_summary: Lefebvre and Hoppe synthesize controllable, deterministic textures through parallel neighborhood matching and multiresolution operations.
project_comparison: The game instead generates seeded painted textures offline. This produces reproducible wood, cloth and plaster without the runtime complexity of exemplar-based synthesis.

title: Animation space: a truly linear framework for character animation
method_summary: Merry, Marais and Gain generalize skeletal subspace deformation while retaining a linear formulation and hardware rendering.
project_comparison: The comparison explains why plain linear blend skinning can lose volume around strongly bent joints. Our constrained animation range and garment shapes mitigate, but do not mathematically eliminate, those artifacts.

title: Building efficient, accurate character skins from examples
method_summary: Mohr and Gleicher fit a compact real-time deformation model to examples exported from richer authoring tools.
project_comparison: The project similarly separates Blender authoring from a small runtime representation. It exports authored transforms directly, rather than fitting examples or reproducing muscle deformation.

title: Skinning mesh animations
method_summary: James and Twigg derive skinning approximations from deformable mesh sequences using automatically chosen transforms and weights.
project_comparison: Their work supports the practicality of GPU matrix palettes. Our 20-bone rig is explicitly authored and hierarchical, so no automatic bone discovery or progressive approximation is needed.
